name: Foia Foia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired Glottolog entry; only ISO change request and Ethnologue — no descriptive material at all.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG 'PNG Language Resources' pages for ffi and mcv and work/abstract pages for the OPD (the Internet Archive 2015).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Historical phonology of proto-Inland Gulf only: 'Stress appears to have been contrastive (cf. /*ka'ɸuto/ "smoke" vs. /*gene'ɸo/ "bandicoot") but has not been reconstructed below.' Sources list names Allen & Keneqa (2006) sketch phonology, Carr (1991, 2006) and Petterson (2014) word lists for Foia Foia.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Unsourced vowel/consonant tables (evidently from the OPD); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2014. Ethnologue 17th ed., entry Minanibai [mcv] (the Internet Archive 2014-09-25).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Allen, Karan & Betty Keneqa. 2006 (available 2010). Foia Foia organised phonology data; Foia Foia, Western Province. Manuscript, 4 pp. SIL PNG (work id 928474531013). Bibisa village, after the Emeti Alphabet Development Workshop, Nov 2006.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.3 heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' is left empty; 'Syllable Patterns: v vc'; phoneme inventory (p b t d k g ʔ m n ɸ f s h l w; i e a ä[ɐ] o u) and example words carry no stress marks. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006/2007. Change Request 2006-095 and Request for New Language Code Element [ffi] Foia Foia (Phil Carr, SIL PNG, 2007-01-30).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identification only (Bibisa village, pop. 178; 73% cognate with Minanibai; only literature a spelling chart/guide and an unpublished 'Report on ADW held at Emeti 2006').

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.7.7.5 (p.512), typological notes on Minanibai after Franklin 1973b: consonant and vowel charts, then verbatim 'No information is available on the suprasegmental system.'

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Other language groups in the Gulf District and adjacent areas. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 261-277. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 7.42 Minanibai (p.270) and 7.46 'Comments on Phonology and Grammar' (p.273): shared consonant/vowel inventory and sound correspondences for Ipiko, Minanibai, Tao-Suamato; nothing on stress or other suprasegmentals.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages foia1236 (Bookkeeping) and mina1274 Minanibai-Foia Foia.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; comment: 'Minanibai [mcv] and Foia Foia [ffi] are the same language (Usher and Suter 2015: 16-17)'. 0 descriptive refs for either code.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Foia Foia'. NewGuineaWorld (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), West Inland Gulf.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phoneme table (12-13 consonants, 5 vowels), 'Neither final consonants nor consonant clusters occur'; correspondence tables quote Petterson (2014) Bibisa and Carr (2006) Pepeha phonetic forms with stress marks in varying positions ('miɾi, mɑˑ'ɸi, mo'moko, nika'na, 'tebere, ki'ɸɑ, 'inutu); no synchronic stress rule is stated.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy & Edgar Suter. 2015. The Anim languages of southern New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 54(1): 110-142.

sources.note: Only refereed modern treatment of Inland Gulf phonology (comparative); pp. 16-17 of the preprint treat Minanibai/Foia Foia and may comment on stress/accent in the family.

sources.citation: Petterson, Robert. 2014. Foeafoea (Foia Foia) of Bibisa village: survey word list, 204 items + 26 phrases, phonetic transcription with stress marks. Unpublished ms., SIL PNG (Ukarumpa).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The fullest phonetic record of Foia Foia with stress marked on every item; an analyst could read a stress pattern off it, and Petterson may have accompanying notes.
